grades.quote: Regardless of whether the comparison results are equal or not, the old memory value is written to the general-purpose register `rd` after sign expansion.
grades.reason: Describes LoongArch AMCAS compare-and-swap, a conditional write that happens only when the old value equals the expected value. It is not an LL/SC loop and gives no diagnosis of repeated failure, so it is only loosely related.

grades.quote: Then a subsequent `WRS.NTO` instruction would cause the hart to temporarily stall execution in a lowpower state until a store occurs to the reservation set or an interrupt is observed.
grades.reason: Covers Zawrs, which stalls a hart on a reservation set in LR-based polling loops. It does not explain why an SC keeps failing, so it is auxiliary context only.

grades.quote: Other processor cores or Cache Coherent I/O masters perform a store operation on the Cache line where the address corresponding to the `LLbit` is located.
grades.reason: Explains LoongArch LL/SC. SC writes only if LLbit is 1, and the passage lists what clears LLbit: ERTN, or another core or coherent I/O master storing to the cache line. It also says a non-Cached access gives an uncertain result. These are direct causes of repeated SC failure in a retry loop.

grades.quote: Unconstrained LR/SC sequences might succeed on some attempts on some implementations, but might never succeed on other implementations.
grades.reason: Explains when RISC-V LR/SC loops are guaranteed to eventually succeed (constrained loops) and when they might never succeed (unconstrained sequences). It also lists the constraints that matter for diagnosing repeated SC failure, such as the instruction limits, same address and size, and the LR/SC eventuality memory region.
